hens_rule_text: Hens allowed with no fixed cap found; the required coop setback grows once you keep more than 6 hens, so 6 or fewer is the simplest tier. No roosters.
permit_notes: No permit requirement was confirmed or ruled out in the sources found; the rules read as development standards in the zoning code rather than a permit program.
setback_notes: Coop set back at least 5 ft from side or rear property lines when keeping 6 or fewer hens, or at least 10 ft from those lines when keeping more than 6; not stated as distance from a neighbor's dwelling.
coop_rules: Hens kept in a coop and pen within a securely fenced rear yard area; coop height capped at 8 ft; coop and pen kept clean and sanitary.
zoning_notes: Standards appear to come from the zoning code's Standards for Specific Land Uses chapter (City of Santa Rosa Code, Chapter 20-42); applicability across all residential zones was not fully confirmed.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of Santa Rosa Code, Chapter 20-42 Standards for Specific Land Uses (eCode360)
BackYard Chickens: Santa Rosa California Chicken Ordinance

research_notes: Facts (rooster ban, tiered 5 ft/10 ft setback by hen count, coop height cap, rear-yard containment) come from a WebSearch extract referencing the City of Santa Rosa zoning code's Chapter 20-42 land use standards; the eCode360 page itself was not opened directly, and no numeric hen cap, code section number, or permit requirement could be confirmed.
